review: The hymn is the finished work: 1:1–4 is John 19:30 (נִשְׁלַם) with 1 Pet 1:19, 2:1–4 is Rom 4:5 with Heb 10:12–14, 3:1–4 is Phil 2:6–8 with John 17:4, 4:1–4 is Heb 4:9–10 with Rom 10:4, 5:1–4 is Isa 64:5 (כַּבֶּגֶד עִדִּים) with 1 Pet 1:7 (בָּאֵשׁ), 6:1–4 is Jas 2:17–26 with Eph 2:8–9, and 7:1–4 is Rom 5:1 with John 3:16.

1:4 אָמַר: נִשְׁלַם — the Arabic قَالَ: «قَدْ كَمَل» quotes the word from the cross; the Hebrew uses נִשְׁלַם, the same verb the Gospel uses of the Scripture being fulfilled, so the line is the accomplishment and not merely a completion.

5:4 יָזֹקּוּ בָּאֵשׁ — the Arabic صُفِّيَتْ بِالنَّار is 'refined by fire'; the Hebrew uses זָקַק, the smelting verb of Job 28:1 and Ps 12:7, because the stanza is testing the works and not destroying them.

6:3–4 keep the print's paradox (works are required, yet they do not pardon) as two bare clauses; the Hebrew does not soften it with a connective, since the stanza's argument depends on the jolt between the lines.
